summary: Astra Health is a web app that helps astronauts log, track and understand their own health during long missions, without depending on a connection to Earth. It brings together eight indicators: heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), SpO₂, blood pressure, glucose, body temperature, sleep and mood. Physiological readings arrive from sensors using the official Bluetooth health profiles (simulated in this prototype); mood is measured with the PANAS questionnaire. Every reading is saved on the device first and gets a preliminary green, yellow or red status, even offline. When a connection is available, the backend compares each reading with the astronaut's own 14-day baseline, flags unusual combinations of indicators with machine learning, and an AI model explains the result in plain language. This matters because the body adapts in space: core temperature rises about 1 °C and blood pressure drops about 8–9 mmHg on long missions, so one fixed threshold for everyone confuses adaptation with illness.
details:
What it does: Astra Health is an offline-first web app that lets astronauts log, track and understand their own health on long missions without depending on Earth. It covers eight indicators: heart rate, HRV, SpO₂, blood pressure, glucose, body temperature, sleep and mood (PANAS questionnaire). Every reading is saved on the device first and gets an immediate green/yellow/red status from clinical thresholds, even with no connection. When a link is available, the backend compares each reading with the astronaut’s own 14-day baseline (z-scores), detects unusual combinations of indicators with an Isolation Forest model, and uses Claude to explain the result in plain language. Crew members see their full history plus their crewmates’ latest status; the mission leader can open crewmates’ history; an admin panel manages crews.

Benefits and impact: Earlier detection of health changes, more crew autonomy when communication with Earth is delayed or lost, and personal baselines that account for adaptation to microgravity instead of generic Earth ranges.

Tools: Python, FastAPI, scikit-learn (Isolation Forest), pandas, Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth), Claude API, HTML/CSS/JavaScript with a service worker and offline queue, Docker and Railway for deployment (astrahealth.cooking). Data: NASA open data (I4 mission) and the MMASH dataset, used to simulate 22 astronauts across short, standard and long missions with pre-flight, flight and post-flight phases.

Creativity: It combines three layers (clinical rules, personal baseline and ML anomaly detection) so it works offline and gets smarter online. The sensors chosen are ones that have actually flown and use standard Bluetooth health profiles (Astroskin, Oura, CGM).

Factors considered: No invented numbers: every threshold is backed by a source (BTS, AHA, ACC/AHA, ESC/ESH, Endocrine Society, Stahn et al.). We also considered exercise context (no temperature or HR alerts while exercising), privacy by role, offline use, and explanations a non-doctor can understand.
